solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fur seen in country with cool interior …

indicators.note: having something as its interior means the cool word sits inside the country word

parts.note: China is a country
to cool is to chill

explanation.surface: A fur coat spotted in some nation where the inside stays cold, the ellipsis leading on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinchilla is the soft grey pelt of a small Andean rodent, prized as a fur.

clue.text: Exultant sound made by spaniel upset bear

indicators.note: the spaniel breed is spoken aloud, its non-rhotic pronunciation giving the first part

parts.note: a cocker is a breed of spaniel

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the bear word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: Pooh is A. A. Milne's bear Winnie-the-Pooh

explanation.surface: A dog barking in triumph after toppling a bear.
explanation.walkthrough: In British, non-rhotic speech the final R of the spaniel name is not pronounced, so it sounds like 'cocka'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cock-a-hoop is an idiom for jubilant, crowing with delight.

clue.text: Dome-shaped dwelling I see during journey

indicators.note: the see word comes during, inside, the journey word

parts.note: a go can be a trip or journey, as in 'on the go'
lo is an old word for see, look

explanation.surface: A traveller spotting a dome-shaped home on the way.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is an Inuit shelter built from snow blocks in a dome shape.

clue.text: Curbable prisoners responsive to instruction

parts.note: cons are convicts, prisoners
trainable means able to be taught

explanation.surface: Inmates who can be controlled because they take direction well.
explanation.definitionFit: Something curbable can be restrained, a synonym for being able to be held in check.

clue.text: Popular drink one duke finds tasteless

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
to sip is to drink
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An aristocrat finds a trendy beverage bland.
explanation.definitionFit: Insipid means lacking flavour, a synonym for bland or without taste.

clue.text: State of roast regularly served up in rented house

indicators.note: the reversed pair goes inside the rented word

parts.note: let means rented out

indicators.note: in a down clue served up means the letters are read upwards, backwards
takes every other letter of roast, the second and fourth

explanation.surface: A joint of roast meat routinely dished up in a rented home.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a country, an independent state, enclosed within South Africa.

clue.text: … being included in one's selection

indicators.note: the letters are contained within the words that follow, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: Continuing the fur clue: the item is among the things you have chosen.
explanation.definitionFit: Esse is the Latin-derived philosophical term for existence or essential nature.

clue.text: Romanians could get in a state in Italy

indicators.note: the Romanians could get in, be fitted into, a different arrangement, signalling their letters reshuffled

explanation.surface: People from Romania could be admitted to an Italian region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a state' also suggests the anagram, but 'a state' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: San Marino is a tiny independent republic surrounded by Italy, so a state within Italy.

clue.text: Grind away before sealing arrangement with bank

indicators.note: the before word seals in, enclosing, the bank arrangement

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
OD stands for overdraft, borrowing agreed with a bank

explanation.surface: Wearing something down before sealing a deal with your bank.
explanation.definitionFit: To erode is to wear away gradually, a synonym for grinding away.

clue.text: Consular agent advances date once familiar to Romans

parts.note: CA is the standard abbreviation for consular agent
to advance money is to lend it

explanation.surface: A diplomat's representative moves a date forward, in a period setting of ancient Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The calends was the first day of each month in the Roman calendar, a named date Romans used.

clue.text: Member of duo taking boy round City function

indicators.note: the boy word goes round the City abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: a son is a boy
EC is the postcode for the City of London
a do is a party or social function

explanation.surface: One half of a pair takes a lad around town to a social event.
explanation.definitionFit: In a piano duet the secondo is the player taking the lower part, one of the two performers.

clue.text: Leader of midland county primarily involved with arts centre

indicators.note: involved means twisted or entangled, so the letters are mixed up
picks the first letter of each of the words of, midland and county

explanation.surface: A head of a Midlands county heavily engaged with a local arts venue.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage the concertmaster is the principal first violinist, the orchestra's leader.

clue.text: Fellow given time to receive oxygen at a height

indicators.note: the fellow-plus-time pair takes in the oxygen symbol, which goes within it

parts.note: Alf is a man's name, standing for any fellow
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A chap granted a spell on breathing apparatus while high up, like a climber or pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloft is a synonym for up high, overhead or in the air.

clue.text: Head accommodating over wine for mogul

indicators.note: the head word accommodates, holding inside it, the other two pieces

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
tent is a deep red Spanish wine, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: A boss making room for more wine for a tycoon.
explanation.definitionFit: A mogul is a powerful magnate, and a potentate is a ruler or person of great power, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Completely finished deliveries and swindled comic at hotel

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries by one bowler
done means cheated, as in 'I've been done'
a wit is a comic person
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A tale of a postal round finished and a comedian conned at his hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something entirely concluded and dealt with, finished for good.

clue.text: Finally leave on excursion with mature followers

indicators.note: takes the final letter of each of the words leave and on

parts.note: a tour is an excursion
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: At last setting off on a trip with grown-up fans.
explanation.definitionFit: An entourage is a group of attendants or hangers-on accompanying someone important.

clue.text: Old peasant managed church bar

parts.note: a hind was historically a farm labourer or peasant
ran means managed, as a business
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A former farmhand ran a pub run by the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar can be an obstacle, and a hindrance is something that obstructs.

clue.text: One thus will hurry to be insistent

definitions.meaning: a driver pressing the accelerator pedal hard speeds up
the idiom also means to refuse firmly and insist on something

explanation.surface: A driver flooring it, and someone digging in their heels.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the literal one: pressing the foot down on the accelerator makes a car go faster.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the same idiom: accelerating in a car and taking a firm stand.

clue.text: Dashes up with a companion to get healthy food

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: nips means dashes, as in nips to the shops
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Someone races upstairs with a friend for a nutritious meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach is a leafy green vegetable famed for its nutritional value.

clue.text: Old couple embracing in French outdoors

indicators.note: the couple word embraces, holding inside, the French word

parts.note: a pair is a couple
en is French for in

explanation.surface: An elderly pair hugging in France in the open.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-air describes something held outside rather than indoors.

clue.text: Tip from tedious person about one going with flow

indicators.note: the flow word goes alongside, placed before the rest

parts.note: to pour is to flow

indicators.note: the tedious person goes about the one, enclosing it

parts.note: a bore is a tedious person
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Advice gained from a dull person on following the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Pourboire is French borrowing for a gratuity given to a waiter, literally money 'for drinking'.

clue.text: Secretary has pounds invested in American song

parts.note: PS stands for private secretary

indicators.note: the pounds symbol is put inside the American abbreviation

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pounds, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: An office assistant has put money into a US tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalm is a sacred song or hymn, as in the Book of Psalms.

clue.text: Person with rod initially lashing out in fury

indicators.note: out tells us a letter is taken away from the fisherman word

parts.note: an angler fishes with a rod

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word lashing

explanation.surface: A fisherman flailing his rod about in a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Anger and fury are synonyms for strong rage.

clue.text: Envious member of political party

definitions.meaning: a member of the environmentalist ... Party

explanation.surface: A jealous politician.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour word means jealous and also names a member of an environmental party.

clue.text: Walk down alley, to begin with, after a game

indicators.note: the first letters come after the earlier pieces

parts.note: a game leg is a lame one

indicators.note: picks the opening letters of the words down and alley

explanation.surface: Instructions to stroll down a back alley after playing a match.
explanation.definitionFit: An alameda is a public promenade or tree-lined walk, a word from Spanish.

clue.text: A horse ultimately kept in London district — a hunter

indicators.note: these letters are held within the district name

parts.note: Acton is a district of west London

indicators.note: picks the last letter of the word horse

explanation.surface: A horse stabled in a London suburb is a hunter, a horse bred for hunting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a hunter' tempts as the horse type, but it is Actaeon, the mythical huntsman.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Actaeon was a huntsman turned into a stag by Artemis and killed by his own hounds.

clue.text: Unpretentious-sounding carriage

indicators.note: the hyphenated sounding says the word for unpretentious is spoken and its sound taken

parts.note: mean can mean humble or lowly, unpretentious

explanation.surface: A plain-looking horse-drawn vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carriage' looks like a vehicle but means bearing or deportment.
explanation.definitionFit: Mien and carriage both mean a person's bearing or manner of holding themselves.

clue.text: Like some missiles — type crossing top of high mountains?

indicators.note: the type word crosses over, straddling, the single letter

parts.note: a sort is a type

indicators.note: picks the first letter of the word high

parts.note: a range is a chain of mountains

explanation.surface: A kind of missile that flies over lofty peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Short-range is a category of missile with limited reach, so it describes some missiles.
